title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
actual_read_scope: Read the complete arXiv HTML v1 (abstract, Sections 1-8, all classification tables, applications, benchmarks, open problems, and the reference list). This is a survey-only extraction: referenced papers were not read.

routes.problem: How a frozen or trained single LLM converts reasoning into plans, search actions, tool calls, and verified execution.
routes.mechanism: In-context workflows interleave thought/action, decomposition, tree or graph search, external tools, and selective retrieval; post-training uses SFT/RL to internalize tool-use and search policies.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct: orchestration, branching, tool observations, and repeated verification change generated-token and interaction-step budgets; the survey does not provide normalized performance-token curves.

routes.problem: How agents improve across episodes or long interactions without full retraining.
routes.mechanism: Verbal reflection, validator feedback, persistent factual/experience memory, structured memory, adaptive context, tool/skill synthesis, and optional parametric updates.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct for memory retrieval, compression, and reflection because they alter context length and number of corrective turns; post-training adaptation is indirect unless deployment-time token use is measured.

routes.problem: How multiple agents divide labor, communicate, coordinate, and evolve toward a shared goal.
routes.mechanism: Fixed role pipelines, LLM-driven topology, theory-of-mind collaboration, graph/policy-based topology generation, shared memory, and multi-agent RL/co-evolution.
routes.inference_token_link: Usually indirect or compute-only: extra agents and messages generally add tokens, while routing, selective activation, and communication compression could reduce them; the survey reports no common token-normalized curves.

routes.problem: Where to place agentic capability: inference-time orchestration with frozen parameters versus capability internalization through SFT/RL.
routes.mechanism: In-context search/workflows spend test-time interaction; post-training optimizes trajectory or tool policies and can reduce reliance on prompts, but incurs training cost.
routes.inference_token_link: Direct conceptual link, but no apples-to-apples cost/performance frontier is supplied; training FLOPs and inference tokens must remain separate.

routes.problem: How agents plan under partial observability and integrate visual, embodied, scientific, or other multimodal state.
routes.mechanism: POMDP/Dec-POMDP framing, external or learned world models, multimodal memory/search, and domain-specific tools and validators.
routes.inference_token_link: Indirect: additional observations, tool calls, and multimodal context can raise token use; world models may reduce trial-and-error, but this survey leaves the token tradeoff unmeasured.

candidates.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
candidates.reason: Canonical in-context tree search over partial thoughts; it exposes the accuracy-versus-search/branching-token tradeoff, but the survey gives no normalized token curve.

candidates.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
candidates.reason: Defines the interleaved thought-action-observation loop; each tool turn changes context and output tokens, while the survey does not quantify efficiency.

candidates.title: REWOO: Decoupling Reasoning from Observations for Efficient Augmented Language Models
candidates.reason: The survey explicitly places it under decoupled planning and labels it efficient; decoupling can reduce repeated observation-conditioned reasoning, but this survey does not reproduce a token curve.

candidates.reason: Self-supervised API-call annotation plus fine-tuning moves tool decisions into model behavior; it is primarily capability/training efficiency evidence, not a deployment token-efficiency result.

candidates.title: Search-R1: Training LLMs to Reason and Leverage Search Engines with Reinforcement Learning
candidates.reason: RL trains iterative search-token actions during reasoning; it directly changes the number of retrieval/trajectory steps, but the survey reports capability framing rather than a token-performance frontier.

candidates.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
candidates.reason: Stores distilled verbal feedback for later trajectories; reflection adds tokens immediately but may reduce repeated failures over episodes. The survey does not isolate either effect in token-normalized results.

candidates.title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
candidates.reason: Evolves a code-skill library from environment feedback and memory; useful for long-horizon adaptation, but embodied observations and skill-generation calls can increase inference tokens and no efficiency curve is given.

candidates.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
candidates.reason: Hierarchical memory/context management is directly relevant to keeping active context bounded; the survey categorizes it but does not report a performance-versus-active-token curve.

candidates.title: LightMem: Lightweight and Efficient Memory-Augmented Generation
candidates.reason: The survey explicitly identifies lightweight/efficient memory-augmented generation; it is a strong candidate for context/token accounting, but this extraction does not verify its original measurements.

candidates.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
candidates.reason: Evolving context is a direct mechanism for reallocating or compressing inference-time tokens across self-improvement; the survey gives no standardized curve or cost accounting.

candidates.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for a Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
candidates.reason: Canonical role-decomposed software pipeline; extra role messages and staged artifacts are a coordination compute/token cost, while the survey offers no token-normalized comparison.

candidates.title: AutoGen: Enabling Next-Gen LLM Applications via Multi-Agent Conversations
candidates.reason: Representative multi-agent conversation orchestration; communication rounds directly consume tokens, but this survey cites it for architecture rather than efficiency evidence.

candidates.title: GPTSwarm: Language Agents as Optimizable Graphs
candidates.reason: Treats agent pipelines as optimizable graphs, linking topology selection to inference orchestration; potential route to selective activation, but no token-performance evidence is summarized.

candidates.title: Optimal-Agent-Selection: State-Aware Routing Framework for Efficient Multi-Agent Collaboration
candidates.reason: The survey explicitly labels state-aware agent selection as efficient; routing fewer agents/messages is directly relevant to inference tokens, but original efficiency results were not read here.

candidates.title: Mem-Gallery: Benchmarking Multimodal Long-Term Conversational Memory for MLLM Agents
candidates.reason: Covers multimodal long-term memory evaluation and therefore tests the boundary where visual/audio memory competes with text context; it is a benchmark, not direct token-efficiency evidence.

candidates.title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
candidates.reason: Primary taxonomy source for single-agent, self-evolving, multi-agent, in-context, and post-training routes; it defines the space but does not itself establish token-efficiency measurements.

gaps_conflicts: The survey's three-layer taxonomy (foundational single-agent, self-evolving, collective multi-agent) is orthogonal to its optimization axis (in-context versus post-training); a method can occupy multiple cells, so categories must not be treated as mutually exclusive.

In-context orchestration directly spends inference tokens and environment/tool turns; post-training changes policy parameters but is mainly a training-compute route. The survey does not supply matched performance-versus-inference-token curves across the two.

Multi-agent collaboration is usually presented as a capability/coordination gain. Communication overhead, repeated shared context, and extra agent calls are acknowledged conceptually, but no common token accounting or Pareto frontier is reported.

Memory, reflection, retrieval, and multimodal/world-model modules can reduce repeated failures or active-context size, yet the survey generally reports qualitative capability and benchmark coverage rather than active-token, total-generated-token, or cost-normalized evidence.

Domain applications (science, robotics, healthcare, web, mathematics) demonstrate agentic workflows and benchmarks, not general efficiency claims. Specialized tools, simulators, and multimodal inputs introduce compute and latency variables that should be kept separate from inference-token efficiency.

The paper is v1 submitted 2026-01-18; its 2026 coverage includes early-2026 memory/benchmark entries such as Mem-Gallery, but no later revisions or post-2026-01-18 developments were present in the read version.
